category_title: Non-verbal students with ASD who use non-verbal requests for help and enjoy sensory play
student_description: Trevor is a 7-year-old non-verbal student with ASD who frequently protests and ignores adults when faced with directive communication or demands. He uniquely requires facilitative strategies—specifically following his lead, labeling his actions, and engaging in sensory/musical play—to successfully increase his shared engagement and vocalizations.

criteria.criterion_name: Integration of Sensory and Musical Play
criteria.rationale: Trevor's communication and vocalizations improve significantly when rough and tumble play, singing, and music are utilized as primary interaction tools.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates singing, music, or rough-and-tumble sensory play as core mediums for building communication skills.

criteria.rationale: Consistent, daily 1:1 sessions are required to fine-tune facilitative strategies and build the value of play over time for Trevor.
criteria.check: The long-term plan establishes a routine of daily, short (e.g., 10-minute) 1:1 interaction sessions focused purely on child-led play.
